extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders and organisations invited to respond to Food Standards Agency consultations; and FSA staff designing consultations
extracted.subtask_description: Official guidance on how the Food Standards Agency conducts consultations and engagement: who to consult, methods to use, document standards, response handling, accessibility and language provisions. Intended to guide both respondents and FSA consultation leads on process and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to consult and evidence-based decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is our duty to ensure that decisions are properly informed, and consulting with those that have an interest is necessary to ensure that our decisions take account of relevant opinions and are evidence based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation is required to inform legislation, guidance and policy decisions so they reflect relevant views and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of consultation topics
rubrics_metrics.description: We consult on changes to food and feed law, including assimilated law, and on policy proposals, including regulatory guidance, that directly impact stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultations are targeted at proposals that have direct impact; this defines what topics will normally trigger consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder selection — who we consult
rubrics_metrics.description: We aim to reach stakeholders that are directly affected, or have specific expertise in the subject under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether proposals might impact specific stakeholder groups, including minority groups or those less likely to respond, and try to involve them in the consultation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt consultation approach to issue and stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: We will adapt our approach to the issue on which we are consulting and the key stakeholders we are trying to engage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose methods and level of formality based on the significance of the issue and characteristics of stakeholders to achieve meaningful engagement throughout decision making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal consultation for significant policy/legislative changes
rubrics_metrics.description: For significant policy and legislative changes we will undertake a formal consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal written consultation is used where appropriate; all such consultations are published on the FSA website and stakeholders are alerted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish consultations and alert stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: We publish all consultations on our website and alert stakeholders to this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures transparency and availability of consultation documents to interested parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of alternative engagement methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal written consultation is not always the most appropriate approach and other engagement methods are better suited to deliver meaningful engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other engagement methods include issuing letters to Interested Parties; face-to-face meetings with individuals or small groups of stakeholders; public meetings; focus groups, professional or social networks; social media and other on-line communication platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and alternative formats
rubrics_metrics.description: We take into account access needs and can provide the consultation documents in alternative formats such as Braille.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider and provide for access requirements to ensure inclusive participation (e.g., alternative formats).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain English and avoid jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: In our consultation documents, we aim to: use plain English and avoid using jargon wherever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write clearly to maximise understanding and lower barriers to participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about what stakeholders can influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Be transparent about what decisions stakeholders can influence, by being clear about the scope of our consultations and what we are seeking views on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit which aspects are for comment and which are already decided, so respondents know the boundaries of influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear information about how to respond and get involved
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear information about how to respond and get involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation documents should include instructions on response channels, deadlines, and any requirements for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an assessment of impact (benefits, costs, risks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an assessment of the impact of any proposals to identify the benefits, costs and risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include Impact Assessments or proportionate estimates (e.g., De Minimis Assessments) to support informed responses and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask specific questions and encourage evidence-based responses
rubrics_metrics.description: We normally ask specific questions to focus attention on key issues and we encourage stakeholders to provide evidence and reasoning to support their views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use targeted questions to elicit focused, substantiated input rather than general commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible methods for receiving responses
rubrics_metrics.description: We aim to be flexible in how we receive consultation responses, including emails and letters but also by phone, or in person at a meeting where stakeholders make clear that they want their views captured as part of the consultation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow multiple submission formats to lower barriers and capture input through the most appropriate channels for stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and timing of response summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: We aim to publish summary reports of responses on our website within three months of the closing date of the consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set an expected timeframe for publishing summaries to promote accountability and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data handling and potential disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Information provided in response to FSA consultation may be subject to publication or release to other parties or to disclosure in accordance with the access to information regimes (FOIA, DPA 2018 and EIR 2004).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full details of how the FSA handles data received through consultation are published in the consultations privacy notice and included within consultations; respondents should be aware their responses may be disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unacceptable responses policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses to consultations that are deemed to be malicious or threatening and/or otherwise inappropriate, including unacceptably offensive or abusive language, are not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such responses may be discarded in their entirety from consideration for the purposes of any FSA consultation process and forwarded to the appropriate authority to take action where we consider they may constitute a criminal offence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welsh language provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate we produce consultations in Welsh as well as English, and we do so simultaneously in accordance with our Welsh Language Scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions to translation are allowed when the document is of a technical nature or aimed at a specialist or limited audience; annexes and Summaries of Responses are not translated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Cabinet Office Consultation Principles and Regulators' Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Our consultation process follows the Cabinet Office Consultation Principles and complies with The Regulators' Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation design and conduct should align with these higher-level government principles and regulatory expectations.
